dehydrated_text:
But you're also competing for graduate school, law school, medical school, and scholarships like the road scholarship. Once you get into Yale, from the first day, it's an endless pursuit of achievement; competition after competition after competition. Wherever you go, you're being judged by someone—professor or classmates—and everyone is looking to outdo each other because it's a winner-takes-all system. This is very traumatic and makes you insecure, leading you to believe life is just like that.

Everyone’s an enemy. I have to achieve and achieve to feel good about myself; otherwise, I’ll be overwhelmed by others. People who graduate from Yale have a deep sense of insecurity, even those from wealthy families. Yale wants people who will be most successful in life—those not satisfied with one million dollars but always seeking billions. The competition starts in high school, where you’re trained for Yale, making it another Hunger Games.

Your parents must adopt different parenting systems. One is healthy: "I love you unconditionally; I'll support and always be here for you." This produces happy, fulfilled, secure individuals likely to become teachers. Alternatively, your parents might say, "I don't have time for you but will reward you with ice cream if you win competitions or get good grades." This system neglects the child while demanding achievement, causing trauma that can motivate some to thrive.

This is meritocracy, set up to destroy America and the world. It started at Harvard but now dominates globally, making it a mess. Yale gives many negative emotions; would I still go there if given a second chance? Probably not because the system doesn't leave much choice for poor people who want to succeed. Before, opportunities existed for success without college; George Washington and Abraham Lincoln are examples of great leaders who didn’t attend Ivy League schools. Today, top positions often require elite education.

I do not plan to send my kids to such a competitive and traumatic environment as the Ivy League.
